what_it_is: How much one crop's yield changes with the crop that grew on the field the year before, beyond the stored soil water that water.py already models. Phase 5, item A.
how_to_read: Every multiplier is a relative yield on a ROTATED field, where the previous crop was a different crop, which is 1.0. 'multiplier' is the value the planner uses; 'low' is the stronger drag and 'high' the weaker one, taken from the sources below (never invented). The planner then re-levels each crop against the county's own mix of previous crops, because the county yields our crop model is fitted to already contain that mix (for example, 57% of irrigated corn in the county follows corn). A pair that is not listed here has no sourced effect and stays at the rotated level.
status_words: verified = the number was read in the named source and the ratio worked out here; rough, unverified = a figure we could not read ourselves

effects.basis: K-State says there is about a 10 percent yield advantage to corn in a corn/soybean rotation over continuous corn (1 / 1.10 = 0.91). At Tribune, western Kansas, limited irrigation, 2013-2019 averages, continuous corn made 176 bu/a against 201 for corn after wheat (176 / 201 = 0.876; difference significant, LSD 17). The weaker of the two, 0.91, is the one used.

sources.name: K-State Research and Extension, No-Till in Kansas: Rotations and Cultural Practices (MF2908), eastern Kansas section
sources.figure: about a 10 percent yield advantage to corn in a corn/soybean rotation as opposed to continuous corn

sources.name: Schlegel and Bond 2020, Alternative Cropping Systems with Limited Irrigation, Kansas Agricultural Experiment Station Research Reports 6(8), Table 2

effects.basis: Parsons, southeast Kansas, 1997-2001 (Kelley 2005, Table 4): second-year sorghum made 88 and 97 bu/a at 75 and 135 lb N against 97 and 102 for sorghum rotated every year with soybeans (0.907 and 0.951, mean 0.93). Hesston, central Kansas (Claassen and Roozeboom 2007): continuous sorghum 1,035 kg/ha under the 5,620 of sorghum rotated with wheat (4,585 / 5,620 = 0.82). Tribune, western Kansas, limited irrigation, 2013-2019: continuous sorghum 135 bu/a against 137 after corn (0.985, not significantly different). The one-repeat-year value, 0.93, is the one used; longer runs of sorghum do worse (Kelley: continuous 0.77 at 75 lb N).

effects.basis: Parsons, southeast Kansas, 1997-2001 (Kelley 2005, Table 3), 5-year average: soybeans rotated every year with sorghum 30.3 bu/a, second-year soybeans 28.2 (0.93), continuous soybeans 24.5 (0.81). Only one Kansas source was found, so there is no weaker value than the second-year one; the high end equals the middle.

effects.basis: Hesston, central Kansas, no-till, 10-year averages (Claassen and Roozeboom 2007): continuous wheat 3,246 kg/ha against 3,965 after soybeans and 3,877 after corn (0.82 and 0.84). Tribune, western Kansas dryland (Schlegel et al. 2019), shown for context and not used: continuous wheat averaged about 60% of wheat after sorghum in a 4-year rotation, a figure that also contains the stored-water loss the planner models separately, so it would count that loss twice. Our own rules already keep wheat after wheat out of the plans; this applies when a farmer scores such a rotation.

not_applied.reason: K-State credits corn after soybeans with 40 lb N an acre (Corn Production Handbook C-560, Table 10). That is fertilizer the farmer does not have to buy, not extra bushels, and the planner's costs are fixed budgets per crop, so it is not counted a second time. The yield side of the same benefit is the corn-after-corn drag above, which re-levels corn after soybeans upward against the county mix.

sources.name: K-State Corn Production Handbook C-560, Table 10, Corn nitrogen credits for various previous crops

not_applied.reason: No Kansas yield figure was found. K-State's nitrogen credit for alfalfa (40 to 120 lb N an acre by stand) is a fertilizer saving, and an old eastern Kansas trial found corn the first year after alfalfa yielded less, believed to be soil moisture used up by the alfalfa. A yield credit would be a guess, so the effect is left out (multiplier 1, the rotated level).
